stemMd: “Our best-performing salesperson follows a detailed morning routine. If every salesperson adopts that routine, all will perform equally well.” Which flaw is most important?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It compares two numerical rates with different units.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It assumes that success cannot be evaluated.

options.label: C
options.textMd: It concludes that routines are impossible to change.

options.label: D
options.textMd: It claims the successful salesperson has no routine.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It assumes that a feature associated with one person’s success is sufficient to reproduce that success in everyone.

explanationMd: Other capabilities, territories, or customer relationships could explain performance, and the routine may not have the same effect for everyone. Association in one case is insufficient for a universal guarantee.

distractorRationale.c: The proposed plan assumes routines can change.
distractorRationale.a: No rates or units are compared.
distractorRationale.b: The reasoning presupposes a performance evaluation.
